clue.text: Musical window-cleaner's aid is highly-strung

parts.note: Cats is the long-running Lloyd Webber stage musical
a cradle is the suspended platform window-cleaners work from on tall buildings

explanation.surface: A stage show turns out to rely on a nervy piece of window-washing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly-strung' is read literally: the children's game is played with string stretched across the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The game consists of loops of string woven between the fingers, so it is literally strung up high.

clue.text: Firm's leaders in rough negotiations will get plastered

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the leaders of the next words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Company bosses in tough talks will end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' suggests drunk; a foot corn gets a corn plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore hard patch of skin on a toe is covered with a medicated plaster.

clue.text: An alternative to meat consumed by worthiest of us?

indicators.note: the answer is eaten up inside these words, across their joins

explanation.surface: A virtuous diner's meat substitute is eaten by the best of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' shows the word lies within 'worthiesT OF Us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd is a protein that vegetarians eat instead of meat.

clue.text: No tea-wagon for the stars?

parts.note: char is slang for tea
less means without, so no
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A space station lacks a trolley for serving tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Char-less wain is a wagon with no tea. CHARLES'S WAIN is the old British name for the Plough (Big Dipper).
explanation.definitionFit: Charles's Wain is a group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major.

clue.text: From members of the choir, one lost out

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of lost are rearranged

explanation.surface: One singer has gone missing from the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LOST into LTOS, after A; 'From' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos sing the low female or high male part in a choir.

clue.text: It's handled for those who look poorly

definitions.text: It's handled for those who look poorly

parts.words: It's handled for those who look poorly
parts.note: a pair of spectacles held up by a handle, for people with weak sight

explanation.surface: Something is brought along for patients who seem unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look poorly' suggests seeming ill but means seeing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: These eyeglasses were held to the eyes by a long side handle by those with weak vision.

clue.text: Piece floating about in soup

indicators.note: things floating about drift into a new order, so the word soup is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is seen bobbing around in a bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floating about' rearranges SOUP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical work or composition is commonly called a piece.

clue.text: Ordinary soldier's leading — it's not naturally explained!

indicators.note: leading means the soldier goes in front of the word for ordinary

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
normal means ordinary

explanation.surface: An ordinary soldier takes charge in a mysterious episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts PARA in front of NORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Supernatural events lie beyond the scope of scientific explanation.

clue.text: She's served you with meals as now, to order

indicators.note: made to order means arranged as wanted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A waitress has brought your meals, cooked as ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' rearranges MEALS AS NOW; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female shop assistant is the person who serves customers.

clue.text: Official line about player that's unruly

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a match official

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the railway letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A match official calls a footballer's behaviour unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RY (railway, a line) round ACTOR, after REF.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes a stubborn person who resists control, a synonym of unruly.

clue.text: Master won't start lesson without written work

indicators.note: the letter for master refuses to begin the word, so it is dropped from the front

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster refuses to begin teaching unless there is no paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: MORAL loses its first letter M (master), as 'won't start' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral examination is spoken rather than set down on paper.

clue.text: Pain with a novel cause?

parts.note: novel suggests new, but it is a book whose writing brings an ache to the hand

explanation.surface: Doctors find an ache with an unusual origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' means unusual in the surface but a book in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's hand muscles can seize up from long periods of handwriting.

clue.text: Uniting to reduce number of taxis?

explanation.surface: Taxi drivers band together to cut down the cabs waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing ranks is the idiom for a group joining together in defence; literally, shutting cab stands cuts the places taxis wait.

clue.text: Bird cut off on a wet stormy run

parts.note: to shear is to cut off, as with wool

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A bird is stranded on a wet and stormy run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges A, WET and R into WATER; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabird skims low over the waves, so it is named for slicing the surface.

clue.text: Trifle with pickle woman served up, lovely with no filling!

parts.note: dill is a herb used for pickles

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word for woman is written upwards

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: lovely without its filling keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trifle with pickle is served by a woman, nice but missing its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns LADY into YDAL; 'with no filling' leaves LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or waste time is to trifle.

clue.text: You'll be sorry and irritated when it's on

definitions.text: You'll be sorry and irritated when it's on

parts.words: You'll be sorry and irritated when it's on
parts.note: a garment of coarse cloth worn as penance: the wearer is sorry for sins and the skin is chafed

explanation.surface: A warning that putting something on will bring regret and annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' is repentance and 'irritated' is the itching skin, both from the penitent's prickly garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitents wore the coarse goat-hair shirt to show contrition while it chafed their skin.

clue.text: Combine to get in variety with speed

indicators.note: variety means making different forms, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone joins a variety show at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges GET IN to INTEG; 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To join parts into one whole is to combine them.

clue.text: Where arms come out, king's being kept in excessively

indicators.note: the king's letters are kept inside the word for excessively

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex), with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A monarch is held captive far longer than he should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept in' puts R'S inside TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the part from which the arms branch out.

clue.text: Shining silver's not very bright

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a low light is dim, not very bright

explanation.surface: Silver gives off a gleam, though only a faint one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing or radiant with light is shining.

clue.text: Attackers from overseas skittled by English bowler

definitions.text: Attackers from overseas skittled by English bowler

parts.words: Attackers from overseas skittled by English bowler
parts.note: the Spanish fleet of 1588, defeated by Sir Francis Drake, famous for finishing his game of bowls first

explanation.surface: A touring cricket side is bowled out cheaply by an English bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: the 'bowler' is Drake, who by legend played bowls on Plymouth Hoe before sailing against the Spanish fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish invasion fleet of 1588 was the overseas attacker beaten by Drake's English navy.

clue.text: Popular tune for a union inauguration

definitions.text: Popular tune for a union inauguration

parts.words: Popular tune for a union inauguration
parts.note: a union here is a marriage, and the familiar tune is played as the couple begin married life

explanation.surface: A well-known song is chosen to open a trade union's new branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but it is a marriage; the tune is Mendelssohn's, played as the newlyweds leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's or Wagner's processional music is played at the start of married life.

clue.text: Tree taken by man from the town hall

indicators.note: the word man is taken away from the councillor

parts.note: an alderman is a senior councillor from the town hall
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree is taken by a council official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' removes MAN from ALDERMAN, a British councillor from the town hall; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing in damp places.

clue.text: Water holder for blackbird

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A water dish is set out for a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackbird' splits into B (black) and OWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep dish holds water, as in a fruit or washing-up bowl.

clue.text: Skills of the man not at the head in a suit

indicators.note: the man's word is not at the head, so it is removed from the front

parts.note: hearts is a suit in a pack of cards
he refers to the man

explanation.surface: A man's talents leave him not at the top in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARTS loses HE at its head; 'of' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafts or accomplishments are called the arts, as in arts and skills.

clue.text: Dead ringer

parts.note: read not as a lookalike but as a bell rung slowly for someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone is the exact double of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead ringer' means a double, but here it is a bell sounded for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is struck slowly in a funeral knell to mark a death.

clue.text: Punishment for lad receiving treatment in dock

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for dock

parts.note: a dock for ships is a harbour

indicators.note: the word lad is treated, worked on, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is given medical care while sitting in the court dock as his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving treatment' turns LAD into DLA; 'in' puts it inside HARBOUR. 'dock' suggests a courtroom but is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour was a prison sentence of heavy physical work.

clue.text: Torpedoes demolish things, we are told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word for demolish is taken by its sound

parts.note: to raze buildings is to demolish them

explanation.surface: Torpedoes are said to destroy whatever they hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torpedoes' are the electric fish; 'we are told' gives the sound of RAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The torpedo is a kind of electric ray, a flat fish that stuns prey.

clue.text: Car cutback is occurring in capital

parts.note: the Metro was a popular British small car

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
taken as written

explanation.surface: Car production is being trimmed in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOP into POL. The Metro was a small Austin car sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital city is the chief city, a large metropolis.
